title: True-up flexible credit model and multi-year commit smoothing playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket delivers a repeatable playbook for enterprise renewals that combines: (1) a flexible true-up / credit mechanism for usage variance, (2) multi-year commit smoothing (graduated discounts that encourage longer commitments without excessive revenue leakage), and (3) standardized contract language and Security Questionnaire responses to accelerate procurement. The output will be a pricing worksheet, templated contract clauses, console billing UI copy for renewals, and an A/B experiment design for measuring impact on retention and expansion velocity.

Background & problem statement:
- Sales and Customer Success report friction at renewal: large swings in usage drive lengthy renegotiations or conservative over-commitments.
- Current true-up process is manual, inconsistent across deals, and creates churn risk or hidden discounts.
- Multi-year discounts are available but lack a disciplined uplift ladder; sales give ad-hoc concessions to close renewals.
- Security Questionnaire answers are sometimes inconsistent between SOWs and the customer portal, increasing legal review time.

Goals & success metrics:
- Reduce renewal negotiation time by 25% (baseline: average 18 days to close renewal after quote).
- Improve 12-month Net Dollar Retention (NDR) by +3 percentage points in cohorts subject to the playbook.
- Decrease percent of renewals requiring legal escalations for bespoke true-up language to <10%.
- Achieve a +6% median ARR uplift on deals that adopt the multi-year smoothing option vs 1-year resets.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) True-up Flex Credit Model (Proposal A - Preferred):
   - Each enterprise contract includes a quarterly usage tolerance band and an automatic credit/charge mechanism.
   - Tolerance bands: +/-10% allowed variation (no charge/credit). Outside band: 
       * 10-25% over commit => prorated true-up charge at list rate * 0.9 (10% discount on overage).
       * >25% over commit => immediate true-up invoiced at list rate (no discount) and triggers quota review.
   - Under-utilization: Customers can bank credits up to 6 months or apply credits to future invoices; credits expire after contract term.
   - Rationale: reduces fear of short-term spikes and removes heavy negotiation overhead.

2) Multi-year Commit Smoothing (Proposal B):
   - Graduated discount ladder to reward longer commitments while protecting revenue:
       * 1-year commit: 0% discount (baseline).
       * 2-year commit: 8% effective discount across term (smoothed monthly pricing).
       * 3-year commit: 15% effective discount across term.
   - Optional mid-term true-up cadence (quarterly) with the same tolerance bands as above.
   - Add a renewal uplift clause that caps incremental discounts on amendment to <= 3% to prevent compounding concessions.

3) Contract & SecQ Templates:
   - Standardized true-up clause (legal-approved) with clear examples and invoicing cadence.
   - Security Questionnaire (SecQ) canonical responses for each pricing tier that map to data handling promises (e.g., dedicated audit log retention for Dedicated customers).
   - Single-liner summaries for sales playbook and a 1-page FAQ for customers.

4) Console/Billing UX changes (small frontend scope):
   - New renewal modal copy that surfaces: commit term, true-up tolerance, expected quarterly cadence, and credit balance.
   - Billing dashboard: show projected true-up exposure and credit bank over last 4 quarters.

Experiment design (A/B test):
- Population: Enterprise customers with upcoming renewals over next 90 days (N ~ 150).
- Arms: Control (current practice), Treatment A (True-up Flex Credit Model + 1-year option), Treatment B (True-up + 2-year commit smoothing).
- Primary metric: time-to-renewal and closed-won renewal ARR uplift at 30 and 90 days post-offer.
- Secondary metrics: legal escalations, CSAT at renewal, % deals adopting multi-year commit.
- Analysis plan: intent-to-treat + per-protocol analyses; use Bayesian estimation to support early stopping if win probability > 95%.

Operational requirements & dependencies:
- Billing system work (ENG-4021): support credit bank ledger, automated quarterly true-up invoicing, and projected exposure calc.
- Console work (ENG-5176): new UI copy and renewal modal, plus hooks for projected exposure.
- Legal review: finalize standard true-up clause and amendment caps.
- Security review (SecOps): validate SecQ canonical answers and map to product commitments.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Discounts lead to long term revenue leakage. Mitigation: smoothing limits and amendment discount caps; pilot with smaller cohort.
- Risk: Billing automation bugs could incorrectly credit/charge customers. Mitigation: staggered rollout, manual approval gate for first 10 customers, and end-to-end test plan.
- Risk: Customers perceive complexity. Mitigation: one-page FAQ, sales training, and pre-built contract language to reduce cognitive load.

Deliverables:
- Pricing worksheet (CSV) with sample math for 20 representative accounts.
- Legal-approved contract addendum text (Doc).
- SecQ canonical answers (Confluence).
- Console renewal UI copy and mock screenshots.
- A/B experiment plan and dashboard (Mode / Metabase link).

proposed_pricing_table: 1-year: no term discount; quarterly true-up tolerance +/-10%
2-year: 8% effective discount across term; quarterly true-up with same tolerance
3-year: 15% effective discount across term; annual true-up optional
True-up overage pricing: 10-25% over commit => list * 0.9; >25% => list rate
Credit bank: credits usable for up to 6 months; expire at contract term end
